working_definition: Dm9 is a wide-field distal medullary amacrine interneuron of the adult Drosophila optic lobe. Its arbors span multiple columns in medulla layers M1 and M6A, with columnar processes in M2 and M5 closely associated with R7 and R8 photoreceptor axons, covering approximately 7 columns per cell. It is glutamatergic, with roughly 110 neurons per hemisphere.

best_match.fbbt_definition: Distal medullary wide-field amacrine neuron with arbors that span multiple columns in layers M1 and M6A and columnar processes between these two layers. The processes in M2 and M5 occupy a central column position and are closely associated with R7 and R8 photoreceptor axons, covering around 7 columns. There are around 110 Dm9 neurons per hemisphere. They are glutamatergic (Davis et al., 2020).

justification: The FBbt term FBbt:00111271 'distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm9' is a precise, non-obsolete term whose definition matches the cluster in every anatomical dimension: wide-field amacrine morphology, medulla layers M1 and M6A, columnar processes in M2/M5 associated with R7/R8, ~7 column coverage, ~110 neurons per hemisphere, and glutamatergic neurotransmitter identity. The cluster label 'Dm9' is the established abbreviation for this exact cell type. No distinguishing features of the cluster fall outside the FBbt definition; no features of the FBbt definition are absent from the cluster description.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Immature form of the distal medullary amacrine neuron Dm9 (Konstantinides et al., 2022). It is a Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron, born from a medulla forming neuroblast during the Hbn/Opa/Slp temporal window (Konstantinides et al., 2022).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: This term represents the immature (developmental) form of Dm9. Kurmangaliyev 2020 is an adult optic lobe atlas; the Dm9 cluster represents the mature adult neuron, not the immature precursor.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Distal medullary wide-field amacrine neuron of the adult optic lobe. Parent class of Dm1-Dm20 subtypes.
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Parent class of the Dm family. Too broad: the cluster is specifically Dm9, not the generic Dm parent, so the subtype-specific term is the correct match.

recommendation: Accept FBbt:00111271 as skos:exactMatch for cluster Dm9. The term is current, precisely defined, and matches all reported anatomical and neurochemical features. No new FBbt term is needed.
